Shiva temple on Umananda (Peacock/Mayur) Island in the middle of the Brahmaputra, claimed to be the world's smallest inhabited river island. Built in 1694 by Bar Phukan Garhganya Handique on the orders of Ahom king Gadadhar Singha (1681-1696), a devout Shaivite. The hill is known as Bhasmachala/Bhasmakuta: per legend Shiva burnt Kamadeva to ashes here with his third eye, and the Kalika Purana says Shiva sprinkled ashes (bhasma) at this spot. The 1897 Assam earthquake destroyed much of the structure, which was rebuilt by a local merchant. CSV town 'Dispur' corrected to Guwahati. Coordinates from Wikipedia (map geocoder placed it incorrectly on the south bank); the temple is on the island in the river.

town_description: Guwahati is the largest city of Assam and the principal city of Northeast India, on the south bank of the Brahmaputra. Once the seat of the ancient kingdom of Pragjyotishpura/Kamarupa, it is the region's main commercial and transport hub and a centre of Shakti worship, with Kamakhya, Umananda and Ugratara shrines.

travel.road: Ferry/motorboat from Uzan Ghat, Kachari Ghat or Umananda Ghat (10-15 minutes); the Guwahati ropeway passes over the island
